question: Should the shared PR template preserve the canonical policy exception that allows contributors to disable maintainer edits when GitHub warns that doing so grants access to fork secrets?
rationale: Exact template parity and contributor secret safety conflict in the current wording, and the permanent cross-repository policy requires a human owner decision.

options.title: Fix canonical, then sync
options.body: Add the Actions/secrets safety exception to the canonical template and update this PR to copy the corrected version.

options.title: Accept unconditional wording
options.body: Keep exact parity and explicitly accept that the template may instruct fork contributors to grant access to their Actions secrets.

recommendation.title: Fix canonical, then sync
recommendation.body: Add the Actions/secrets safety exception to the canonical template and update this PR to copy the corrected version.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant exception is defined in the canonical OpenClaw repository policy, making its adjacent policy owner the best available decision route.
